title: Southern Sweet Tea with Lemon and Mint
summary: Black tea steeps for 5 minutes, sugar and lemon juice are stirred into the hot tea, then it is diluted with cold water and ice, chilled and served with lemon and mint.

steps.title: Steep
steps.text: Pour the boiled water over the tea bags in the heatproof jug and leave for exactly 5 minutes. Lift out the bags, pressing them gently against the side, and discard.

steps.title: Sweeten while hot
steps.text: Stir in the sugar while the tea is still hot until it has completely dissolved; it won't dissolve properly once cold. Stir in the lemon juice.

steps.title: Dilute
steps.text: Pour into the pitcher, add the cold water and about 300 g of the ice and stir. Taste and add a little more sugar if you like it sweeter.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour until cold through.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Pour over the remaining ice in tall glasses and add a lemon round and a mint sprig.

tips: Don't squeeze the tea bags hard; it pushes bitter tannins into the tea.
Adding ice straight away cools the tea quickly and helps keep it clear.
Traditional Southern sweet tea is much sweeter; add up to 50 g more sugar if you want the real thing.
For decaffeinated sweet tea, use decaf black tea bags with the same method.
storage: Keeps covered in the fridge for up to 2 days. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
